newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sees 1997 net grain output of 77-79 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees 1997 net grain output of 77-79 mln T.

text.p: Russian Agriculture Minister Viktor Khlystun said on Friday net grain output this year would rise to 77-79 million tonnes.

"We expect 77 to 79 million tonnes," he told a news conference. Previous government forecasts had been in a range of 70-75 million tonnes, with some officials predicting 80 million tonnes. Last year's net grain output was 69.3 million tonnes, the second poor showing in a row.
Khlystun said grain quality in some regions was significantly better this year.
"This is very important -- we will get more quality grain this year," he said. Quality levels in the grain belt Kuban region in the northern Caucasus had doubled from 1996 levels, he said.

Russia had threshed 35 million tonnes of grain so far, 22 percent below last year's level. Khlystun blamed a late spring, a delayed growing period and what he termed a significant worsening of fuel and equipment supply levels. But he said Russia would have grain to export.

"We are constantly developing our export potential and it will increase this year," he said. Russian imports of wheat and wheat flour, mostly from Kazakhstan and Ukraine, have been steady in recent years, and official figures suggest Russia has a flat grain trade balance.
